checks_run.procedure: Review the product diff since round 15 and the full files it touches: the identity generation (FE14) and its effect on sign-in/out, CSRF, OIDC returnTo, the bilingual messages and FE10-FE13. Scan the non-test diff for risky patterns.
checks_run.command: git diff ed80b23 e3b2375 -- apps packages; aux-checks.sh (diff-scan.log)
checks_run.expected: No regression in auth, CSRF, returnTo, i18n or FE10-FE13; no CDN, secret, eval or innerHTML; a normal same-identity write still updates the cache and navigates.
checks_run.actual:
Assignment discrepancy, disclosed: the named range fe22d759..cbdb4f68 is the round-10->11 change, already reviewed in rounds 11-15 (stat recorded in diff-scan.log). The product change since round 15 is ed80b23..e3b2375: 22 files, apps/web only, +785/-34, of which 569 lines are a new test.

The risky-pattern grep over the non-test diff found no matches. (Its grep exit 1, 'no match', is inside the block; the block records exit 0.) No new string is user-facing: SessionChangedError is silent and never rendered (ErrorState returns null), so there is no bilingual gap.

The client's generation logic is correct. sentGeneration is captured before fetch and checked on every exit path. The generation moves BEFORE the reset hooks in endSession, markSignedOut and noteSessionIdentity. A stale 401 cannot end the new identity. AbortError is still rethrown as before.

Unchanged:
- Sign-out (Shell.tsx): the logout answer is awaited, then markSignedOut.
- LoginPage: on a SessionChangedError it only skips the error banner; returnTo handling is unchanged.
- CSRF: the token is still per session; the server stores sha256(csrf) per session and compares in constant time (sessions.ts).

revalidateSessionFirst is bounded: one shared run per QueryClient, with /me deduplicated (cancelRefetch false). It makes no page refetch unless /me answered and the phase is still active. TanStack's own refetchOnWindowFocus/refetchOnReconnect are off.

The QueryState and RequireSession refetch on SessionChangedError is bounded: once per errorUpdatedAt.

One class residual: success handlers that navigate after a further await (create, edit, org create, user create) are not re-checked. See SEC-R16-19 and the F-DG2-530 verification.

checks_run.procedure:
New class probe zz-sec-r16-web-probe.test.tsx (sha256 f0d72881). It checks four cases:
- Y1: a create of A's whose success continuation runs after the tab moved to B.
- Y1c: the same-identity control.
- Y4: X6 with the production QUERY_DEFAULTS.
- Y5: an observation, in-app navigation without a focus event.
The source review also covered writes (all api.send callers), uploads (EvidencePage UploadDialog through apiRequest), downloads (a plain <a download> link, server-authorised, no client cache), optimistic-concurrency conflict paths (useVersionedSave, RecordForm, EditPage, DefinePage) and the setQueryData sites.
checks_run.environment: $TMPDIR/r16p at f4242ae + probe files; Node 22.22.2 LANG unset, and Node 24.21.0 LANG=C.UTF-8
checks_run.expected: No answer to a request sent under A is written, navigated on or shown after the tab moved to B.
checks_run.actual:
Exit 1 on both runtimes. This is the probe's design: Y1 FAILS. Y1c, Y4 and Y5 pass.

The one failing assertion is `expect(path).not.toBe('/transformations/<A's new id>')` (zz-sec-r16-web-probe.test.tsx:133). The logged line shows: generation 0 -> 1; header B=true; B sees A's code=true and name=true. The page shows 'TR-A-NEW-SECRET · A-CREATED-SECRET-NAME was saved as a draft...' (CreatedNotVisible, rendered from router state).

Mechanism: TransformationCreatePage.tsx:186-201. The POST answer is gated, but the handler then awaits invalidateQueries and a /me refresh. That /me discovers B, and the handler still navigates with A's code and name in router state.

The same navigate-after-await pattern, with no data shown, is at TransformationEditPage.tsx:131-133, OrganizationsPage.tsx:157-159 and UsersPage.tsx:292-294.

The log's only error line is that AssertionError.

Y4: requests on refocus [GET /me, GET business-units, GET transformations]; header B with B's row.

Y5 (observation, not raised): an in-app navigation with no focus event fetches the new page's data with B's cookie under A's header until the next /me. B's own data only; A's CSRF token is refused for any write.

Uploads, conflict paths and setQueryData sites are all gated by the client generation. No optimistic (onMutate) updates exist.

This residual is recorded against F-DG2-530 (verification FAIL) rather than as a new id.

summary: FAIL, on one ground only: F-DG2-530 does not verify CLOSED. FE14's session generation in the API client is genuine. My round-15 reproduction (X3) is fixed, a stale 401 no longer ends the new identity, and X6 holds with production defaults (/me first on refocus). FE10/FE13 also still hold: one navigation, bounded /me, no stale shell, 403 never an end, safe returnTo, same-person drafts kept. But the fix gates only each request's own answer. TransformationCreatePage's success handler awaits a /me refresh after A's 201; when that /me finds B (A signed out and B signed in elsewhere while the POST was in flight), it still navigates with A's code and name in router state, and B sees 'TR-A-NEW-SECRET · A-CREATED-SECRET-NAME was saved as a draft' (probe Y1, Node 22 and 24). That is inside F-DG2-530's expected result, so the finding stays OPEN, Low, not mandatory. Every required check ran and passed: typecheck, build, lint, openapi-lint (161 ops), no-cdn, format, unit 892/892 on Node 22, Node 24 and under load, integration 612/612 in both locale runs with every named suite, migrations 0001-0019, the AUD-403 sweep 146/146, and validate --historical DG0/DG1. No new finding ids are raised.
